title: Moten's New York visit and the battle of bands tours
summary: Jones says Walter Page joined Moten in 1932 and describes five-band battle-of-bands tours with Chick Webb and others.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Beautiful. So we got this band now in Kansas City and Bennie's got his band going. What happened then? How did that band - you say in 1930 Bennie Moten
brought that band to New York and Walter Page - was Basie in that band that came here?

Walter Page did not join it till 1932. When Bennie came to New York City he upset New York City with "Driving Me Crazy," which was Moten's Swing they played, then. And that's the time when they had the 5-band tour with Blanche Calloway, Johnson (Happy Pals) (Hakapais?), Chick Webb. Everybody would get in the buses and make the tour down through . . . . . . You know how things were. You have somebody go around and say, "There's going to be a battle of bands," and the musicians just splitting up the money. You figure out which town and naturally when Chick is going to get to Baltimore - he's born in Baltimore - he's supposed to be the big man there. Everybody is going for broke to try to outdo everybody. That was for the benefit of the customer. Everybody knew who was the best band and it [was] let the public decide. As long as you had it controversial you didn't care. Say I'm going to kick Milt's teeth out when I get him on that bass and everybody'd be looking for me and you - all right, it's a battle. What do you think about Joe Frazier and those other people? So they made 5 million dollars. So what? Everybody's going to come and bet battle, so you split the money. We know who was the best, who's on the bandstand, but we are trying to work because we're coming out of Depression now.
